Q. Q. 1 عَلْبَى , said of a man, His عَلَبِىّ [or rather عِلْبَاآنِ, the former being pl., and the latter dual, of عِلْبَآء, q. v.,] became apparent, by reason of old age: (O, K:) or accord. to the T, his عِلْبَآء became depressed. (TA.) ＝
-A2- عَلْبَاهُ He cut his عِلْبَآء [q. v.], (O, K, TA,) i. e., his slave's علباء: (K, TA:) or he perforated his (i. e. his slave's) علباء, (K, TA,) and put into it a string, or thread. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
